requirements.requirement: Establish a persistent integrity baseline covering /etc on node1.
requirements.summary: AIDE was configured with a validated broad `/etc NORMAL` rule, initialized with 36,014 entries, promoted to a protected active database, and produced a clean initial and post-restart check.

requirements.requirement: Enable later changes under /etc to be identified and reported.
requirements.summary: A controlled change to `/etc/issue` was reported as exactly one changed entry with size and hash differences. Restoring the file returned AIDE to a clean result.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel, using compatible software.
requirements.summary: AIDE 0.19.2 and its nettle dependency came from enabled signed RHEL 10 repositories. Before and after observations show RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 remained unchanged.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Node1 has a persistent, clean AIDE baseline for `/etc`, demonstrated detection and reporting of a later file change, and retained its original RHEL release and kernel. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered services and baseline data were directly observed and agree with the lifecycle snapshots.
limitations: Change detection was behaviorally tested on one representative `/etc` file; coverage of the remainder is established by the validated broad `/etc NORMAL` policy and initialized database rather than individual change tests for every entry.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Package installation supported the baseline (`cmd-c9ff6e93a5314626`); policy and database creation were necessary implementation actions (`cmd-fdfcf83cb0fd4afa`, `cmd-149420a58b6e48ba`, `cmd-575207941aca4c0c`); the bounded detection test was fully restored and its backup removed (`cmd-609a07d3a7744362`, `cmd-cbf3042b61264005`); and the reboot mutation served the mandatory evidence protocol and left no transient-unit residue (`cmd-933d35ac9adf456b`). Final evidence shows no failed services, unchanged listening endpoints, enforcing SELinux, healthy package management, and no abandoned test files (`cmd-d73484606b2449d1`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node1:listening-sockets`, `global:after_executor:node1:package-health`).
